editorial:
Imagine being trapped in a cold, gray hospital back in the 1950s, watching your own brother slowly lose his mind. You are Alexandre, and your whole world revolves around trying to help Elias, who is getting worse by the day. The vibe here is heavy and sad, but it keeps you glued to the screen because you just want to know if Elias will ever come back to his old self. It feels like a race against time, and the way the director shows the creepy hospital makes you feel like you are right there in the room with them.

The acting is where this movie really wins, as the bond between the two brothers feels totally real. While the middle part drags a bit, the emotional payoff at the end makes it worth the wait. If you love stories that pull at your heartstrings and make you think about family, you need to see this. You should definitely stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to catch all the detail, or you can rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night. If you are a collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great call.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, you find out that Alexandre has been imagining parts of the hospital to cope with the pain. He realizes that the only way to save Elias is to face the truth about their past trauma. The twist shows that Elias was actually trying to protect Alexandre all along. In the end, they both find a way to leave the facility together, finally finding peace and healing after years of suffering.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves deep family dramas and emotional stories.
